# Tabs

> Switch between peer panels of one object, with no JS: hidden radios drive the panels.

- Type: Component (disclosure, Navigation)
- Namespace: `ui.tabs`
- Source: `src/ui/tabs.cljc`
- Public fns: `tabs-class-list`, `tabs-classes`, `tabs`
- Keywords: tabs, tab panel, segmented, underline tabs, css only

## When to use

- Peer panels of one object: Overview, Activity, Settings.
- Content that should switch in place without a route change, on all targets including server-rendered hiccup.

## When not to use

- Use button-group for two to five views of the same data (a range or a layout toggle).
- Use accordion for stacked sections that are read in order.
- Use real links when each panel is its own page.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.tabs :as tabs])

(tabs/tabs {:variant :line
            :default "account"
            :tabs [{:id "account"  :label "Account"  :content [:div "..."]}
                   {:id "password" :label "Password" :content [:div "..."]}]})
```

## Examples

### Boxed segmented tabs with a fixed radio name

```clojure
(tabs/tabs {:name "view"
            :tabs [{:id "grid" :label "Grid" :content grid}
                   {:id "list" :label "List" :content list}]})
```

## API reference

### `tabs`

Renders a radio group of triggers and the matching panels. The active tab is uncontrolled; the browser tracks it.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:variant` | `:boxed \| :line` | `:boxed` | :boxed is a segmented control with a raised pill; :line is underlined tabs. |
| `:default` | `string \| keyword` | – | Id of the initially active tab; defaults to the first. |
| `:tabs` | `vector of {:id :label :content}` | – | The tabs. :content is hiccup. |
| `:name` | `string` | – | Radio group name. Auto-generated when omitted; pass one for deterministic markup (tests, SSR snapshots). |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – | Attributes on the root element. |

### `tabs-classes`

Class string for {:variant}.

### `tabs-class-list`

Vector form.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys | Move between tabs (native radio behavior). |
| Tab | Moves focus into and out of the tab list. |

## Accessibility

- Triggers are labels for radio inputs; the focus ring is drawn on the label of the focused radio.
- Panels are hidden with CSS :has(), so hidden content is not read.

## Motion

- Trigger color and background change over --duration-fast; no sliding indicator.

## Responsive behavior

- The tab list wraps; keep labels short. For many tabs prefer a select on phones.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Works without JS. State is not observable server-side.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: Uncontrolled: to react to the active tab, listen for change on the radios via :attrs or render your own triggers.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Same as Replicant; pass :name to keep ids stable across re-renders.

## Notes for AI

- Tabs need no state; do not add an active-tab atom unless you must react to changes.
- For a range toggle (7d, 30d, 90d) use button-group, not tabs.

## Related

- [Button group](button-group.md): Related actions as one segmented control: ghost or boxed, with icon items, counts and separators.
- [Accordion](accordion.md): Progressively reveal supporting content in place, using native details and summary with no JS.
- [Toolbar](toolbar.md): A pill-shaped container that groups icon buttons with separators, horizontal or vertical, optionally floating in a popover.

## Guidance for AI tools

Tabs: Switch between peer panels of one object, with no JS: hidden radios drive the panels. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Tag input

> Turns short text into removable tags with a filtered suggestion dropdown; fully controlled by the host.

- Type: Component (inputs, Selection)
- Namespace: `ui.tag-input`
- Source: `src/ui/tag_input.cljc`
- Public fns: `tag-input-class-list`, `tag-input-classes`, `tag-pill-class-list`, `tag-pill-classes`, `tag-pill`, `tag-dropdown-item`, `tag-dropdown`, `tag-input`, `filter-tags`
- Keywords: tag input, multi-select, tokens, chips input, autocomplete

## When to use

- Several values from a known list (labels, people, categories) in a form.
- Free-text tags where each entry becomes a removable pill.

## When not to use

- Use select for exactly one value.
- Use chip for a small fixed set of filters shown all at once.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.tag-input :as tag-input])

(tag-input/tag-input {:tags selected
                      :input-value query
                      :open (seq suggestions)
                      :filtered-items suggestions
                      :active-index active
                      :placeholder "Add label…"
                      :on-input set-query!
                      :on-select add-tag!
                      :on-remove remove-tag!
                      :on-backspace remove-last!
                      :on-key-down handle-key!})
```

## Examples

### Filtering suggestions

```clojure
(tag-input/filter-tags all-tags selected query) ; excludes selected, matches case-insensitively
```

## API reference

### `tag-input`

The field: selected tag pills, a text input and the dropdown. All state lives in the host.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:tags` | `vector of {:label :value}` | – | Selected tags. |
| `:input-value` | `string` | – |  |
| `:open` | `boolean` | – | Show the dropdown. |
| `:filtered-items` | `vector` | – | Suggestions to show (already filtered). |
| `:active-index` | `int` | – | Highlighted suggestion. |
| `:placeholder` | `string` | `"Add tag..."` |  |
| `:disabled` | `boolean` | – |  |
| `:on-input` | `fn [value]` | – |  |
| `:on-remove` | `fn [tag]` | – |  |
| `:on-select` | `fn [item]` | – |  |
| `:on-backspace` | `fn []` | – | Backspace on an empty input. |
| `:on-clear` | `fn []` | – |  |
| `:on-focus` | `fn []` | – |  |
| `:on-blur` | `fn []` | – |  |
| `:on-key-down` | `fn [key-code]` | – | Arrow and Enter handling. |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `tag-pill`

One selected tag with a remove button.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:label` | `string` | – |  |
| `:on-remove` | `fn` | – |  |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `tag-dropdown`

The suggestion list.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:open` | `boolean` | – |  |
| `:items` | `vector` | – |  |
| `:on-select` | `fn` | – |  |
| `:active-index` | `int` | – |  |
| `:empty-text` | `string` | – |  |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `tag-dropdown-item`

One suggestion row.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:label` | `string` | – |  |
| `:on-select` | `fn` | – |  |
| `:active` | `boolean` | – |  |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `tag-input-classes`

Class string for {:focused :disabled}.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Type | Filters suggestions. |
| ArrowUp / ArrowDown | Move the highlight (host handles :on-key-down). |
| Enter | Adds the highlighted suggestion. |
| Backspace on empty | Removes the last tag. |

## Accessibility

- Pills have remove buttons with labels; the dropdown items are buttons. Give the field a label with form-field.

## Motion

- Focus ring and dropdown fade over --duration-fast.

## Responsive behavior

- Pills wrap inside the field; the dropdown is capped and scrolls.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Renders the current state statically; no interaction without app JS.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: Controlled; keep tags, query, open and active index in state.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Controlled; filter-tags is available on all targets.

## Notes for AI

- The component owns no state; wire every callback or use a small reducer in the host.

## Related

- [Select](select.md): A compact choice field with a framework-drawn listbox, keyboard navigation and form support.
- [Chip](chip.md): A small selectable pill for filters, tags and presets, with an optional color dot.
- [Form](form.md): Labeled fields, inputs, textareas, checkboxes, radios, file and range inputs, joined groups and a search bar.

## Guidance for AI tools

Tag input: Turns short text into removable tags with a filtered suggestion dropdown; fully controlled by the host. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Theme toggle

> A three-way segmented control for light, system and dark appearance, hydrated by the JS runtime.

- Type: Component (actions, Buttons)
- Namespace: `ui.theme-toggle`
- Source: `src/ui/theme_toggle.cljc`
- Public fns: `theme-toggle-class-list`, `theme-toggle-classes`, `theme-toggle`
- JS runtime: `ui.js.theme` (bundled in ui-runtime.js)
- Keywords: theme switcher, dark mode, light mode, appearance, color scheme

## When to use

- An appearance setting in a sidebar footer, header or settings page.

## When not to use

- Use switch for a plain two-state setting that is not the color scheme.
- Do not place more than one theme toggle on a page.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.theme-toggle :as theme-toggle])

(theme-toggle/theme-toggle {:mode "auto"})
```

## Examples

### Controlled in Replicant or Squint

```clojure
(theme-toggle/theme-toggle {:mode theme :on-change set-theme! :size :sm})
```

## API reference

### `theme-toggle`

A radiogroup of three icon buttons (sun, monitor, moon). The runtime module applies data-theme on <html> and persists the choice.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:mode` | `"light" \| "auto" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` |  |
| `:on-change` | `fn [mode]` | – | :cljs and :squint; receives the new mode string. |
| `:size` | `:sm \| :md` | `:md` |  |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `theme-toggle-classes`

Class string for {:size}.

### `theme-toggle-class-list`

Vector form.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Arrow keys | Move between the three options. |
| Enter / Space | Selects. |

## Accessibility

- role=radiogroup labeled Theme; each option has role=radio with aria-checked and a label.

## Motion

- The active pill changes over --duration-fast.

## Responsive behavior

- Fixed size; :sm fits a sidebar footer.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Markup only; ui-runtime.js wires the clicks and persistence.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: Pass :mode and :on-change, or let the runtime handle it.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Same as Replicant.

## Notes for AI

- Themes are data-theme on <html>; accents are data-accent. The toggle only changes the theme.

## Related

- [Switch](switch.md): A toggle for a setting that takes effect immediately.
- [Button group](button-group.md): Related actions as one segmented control: ghost or boxed, with icon items, counts and separators.
- [Sidebar](sidebar.md): An app shell: a sticky sidebar with brand, search, grouped menus, collapsible sections, user footer and a mobile drawer, next to the main area.

## Guidance for AI tools

Theme toggle: A three-way segmented control for light, system and dark appearance, hydrated by the JS runtime. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Editing timeline

> A media editing timeline: a scrubbable ruler, labeled tracks with draggable and trimmable segments, a playhead and a floating transport.

- Type: Component (media, Media)
- Namespace: `ui.timeline`
- Source: `src/ui/timeline.cljc`
- Public fns: `total-time`, `tick-step`, `ticks`, `time->pct`, `span->pct`, `format-time`, `format-readout`, `timeline-class-list`, `timeline-classes`, `dragging?`, `timeline`
- Keywords: timeline, video editor, segments, scrub, playhead, trim

## When to use

- Editing clips, zoom ranges or keyframes against a media duration.
- Scrubbing a playhead with keyboard nudges and snapping.

## When not to use

- Use player-bar for playback without editing.
- For an activity feed (events newest first) build a list, this timeline is not that.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.timeline :as timeline])

(timeline/timeline {:duration 12.5 :current 4.2 :playing false
                    :tracks [{:id :clip :label "Clip" :segments [{:id 1 :start 0.8 :end 11.4 :label "video.mp4"}]}
                             {:id :zoom :label "Zoom" :segments [{:id 2 :start 3.5 :end 6.2} {:id 3 :start 7.6 :end 9.1}]}]
                    :on-seek seek! :on-segment-change edit! :on-play-pause toggle!})
```

## API reference

### `timeline`

Controlled: renders from props and reports edits through callbacks. Interactive on Squint only; other targets render it static.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:duration` | `seconds` | – | Required. |
| `:current` | `seconds` | – |  |
| `:tracks` | `vector of {:id :label :segments [{:id :start :end :label}]}` | – |  |
| `:playing` | `boolean` | – |  |
| `:loop` | `boolean` | – |  |
| `:transport` | `boolean` | `true` | false hides the transport. |
| `:min-gap` | `seconds` | `0` |  |
| `:step` | `seconds` | `0.1` |  |
| `:big-step` | `seconds` | `1` |  |
| `:on-seek` | `fn [t]` | – | Ruler click or drag and keyboard; shift snaps to segment edges. |
| `:on-segment-change` | `fn [{:track-id :segment-id :start :end :edge :phase}]` | – | :phase is :drag or :commit; persist on :commit. |
| `:on-play-pause` | `fn` | – |  |
| `:on-skip-start` | `fn` | – |  |
| `:on-loop` | `fn` | – |  |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `ticks`

Tick times for a duration.

### `format-time`

Tick label format (m:ss or seconds).

### `format-readout`

Transport readout, e.g. 1:23 / 4:56.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| ArrowLeft / ArrowRight | Nudge the playhead or focused segment by :step (Shift for :big-step). |
| Space | Play or pause from the transport. |

## Accessibility

- Segments and the ruler are focusable with keyboard editing; values are announced through the readout.

## Motion

- Segments follow the pointer directly; the playhead has no easing. Snapping highlights over --duration-fast.

## Responsive behavior

- The ruler fills its width; on narrow screens long timelines get fewer ticks.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Static rendering of the current state.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: Static rendering; interaction is Squint only for now.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Fully interactive.

## Notes for AI

- Persist segment edits only on :phase :commit; :drag fires continuously.

## Related

- [Player bar](player-bar.md): A music player bar with artwork, track info, transport controls, a scrubbable progress track and volume.
- [Progress](progress.md): Shows how much of a known task is complete as a filled track.

## Guidance for AI tools

Editing timeline: A media editing timeline: a scrubbable ruler, labeled tracks with draggable and trimmable segments, a playhead and a floating transport. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Toast

> A brief floating confirmation for completed background work, shown by the JS runtime on every target.

- Type: Component (feedback, Messages)
- Namespace: `ui.toast`
- Source: `src/ui/toast.cljc`
- Public fns: `toast-class-list`, `toast-classes`, `toast`, `toast-flash`, `show-toast!`
- JS runtime: `ui.js.toast` (bundled in ui-runtime.js)
- Keywords: toast, notification, snackbar, flash message, htmx

## When to use

- Result of background work: an export finished, a sync failed, a message was sent.
- Server-rendered and HTMX responses that need a confirmation after a swap (toast-flash).

## When not to use

- Confirm foreground actions in place (the button label, the row, the value); never as the only confirmation.
- Use alert for a message that must stay until resolved.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.toast :as toast])

;; Replicant / Squint
(toast/show-toast! {:message "Export finished" :variant :success})

;; Hiccup / HTMX: include the marker in the response fragment
(toast/toast-flash {:message "Saved" :variant :success})
```

## Examples

### Sticky error

```clojure
(toast/show-toast! {:message "Sync failed. Retry from Settings." :variant :danger :duration 0})
```

## API reference

### `toast-flash`

Invisible marker element the runtime consumes and shows as a floating toast. Works inside hx-swap-oob fragments.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:message` | `string` | – | Toast text (required). |
| `:variant` | `:info \| :success \| :warning \| :danger` | `:info` |  |
| `:duration` | `ms` | `5000` | 0 keeps the toast until dismissed. |

### `toast`

Static toast element for previews; the runtime renders real toasts into its own container.

Children: Toast content.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:variant` | `:info \| :success \| :warning \| :danger` | – |  |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `toast-classes`

Class string for {:variant}.

### `toast-class-list`

Vector form.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Click / tap | Dismisses a toast early. |

## Accessibility

- The runtime container is a polite live region, so new toasts are announced.
- Keep messages to one sentence; include the next step for errors.

## Motion

- Toasts slide in over --duration-standard with --ease-enter and fade out; reduced motion fades only.

## Responsive behavior

- Toasts stack at the bottom edge and are full width on phones.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Use toast-flash in the page or an HTMX fragment; needs ui-runtime.js.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: Call show-toast!; it is a no-op when the runtime is missing.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Same as Replicant.

## Notes for AI

- A toast never carries the only copy of an error; errors that need action use alert.
- Success toasts are a label change in words: Export finished, not Success!

## Related

- [Alert](alert.md): A persistent inline message with a tone, icon and optional title that helps people recover or continue.
- [Processing bar](processing-bar.md): A compact accent-bordered panel listing background jobs in progress with thumbnails, labels and spinners.
- [Dialog](dialog.md): A focused modal surface for decisions that need attention, as a native <dialog> or an overlay for reactive apps.

## Guidance for AI tools

Toast: A brief floating confirmation for completed background work, shown by the JS runtime on every target. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Toolbar

> A pill-shaped container that groups icon buttons with separators, horizontal or vertical, optionally floating in a popover.

- Type: Component (layout, Layout)
- Namespace: `ui.toolbar`
- Source: `src/ui/toolbar.cljc`
- Public fns: `toolbar-class-list`, `toolbar-classes`, `toolbar`, `toolbar-separator`
- Keywords: toolbar, floating toolbar, icon buttons, editor toolbar

## When to use

- A cluster of independent icon actions that should read as one surface: formatting, zoom, map controls.
- A floating toolbar anchored to a selection or trigger (inside a popover-content with popover-content--flush).

## When not to use

- Use button-group when the buttons are a choice (one active).
- Use a header with button for a page's primary actions.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.toolbar :as toolbar])

(toolbar/toolbar {}
  (button/button {:variant :ghost :icon :edit :attrs {:aria-label "Edit"}})
  (button/button {:variant :ghost :icon :copy :attrs {:aria-label "Copy"}})
  (toolbar/toolbar-separator {})
  (button/button {:variant :ghost :icon :trash :attrs {:aria-label "Delete"}}))
```

## Examples

### Vertical zoom controls

```clojure
(toolbar/toolbar {:orientation :vertical}
  (button/button {:variant :ghost :icon :plus :attrs {:aria-label "Zoom in"}})
  (button/button {:variant :ghost :icon :minus :attrs {:aria-label "Zoom out"}})
  (toolbar/toolbar-separator {})
  (button/button {:variant :ghost :icon :search :attrs {:aria-label "Fit"}}))
```

## API reference

### `toolbar`

The container (role=toolbar) with a pill radius and a border; buttons inside are clipped to the pill.

Children: Buttons and toolbar-separator elements.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:orientation` | `:horizontal \| :vertical` | `:horizontal` |  |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – | Add aria-label to name the toolbar. |

### `toolbar-separator`

Divider perpendicular to the toolbar flow.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

### `toolbar-classes`

Class string for {:orientation}.

### `toolbar-class-list`

Vector form.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves through the buttons. |

## Accessibility

- role=toolbar with aria-orientation; every icon button needs an aria-label.

## Motion

- None on the container; buttons keep their press feedback.

## Responsive behavior

- Horizontal toolbars do not wrap; split long ones with separators or move overflow into a context menu.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Static markup.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: :class may be a vector.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Static markup.

## Notes for AI

- Use :variant :ghost buttons inside; the toolbar provides the surface.

## Related

- [Button](button.md): A single action with quiet secondary states, press feedback and a loading spinner.
- [Button group](button-group.md): Related actions as one segmented control: ghost or boxed, with icon items, counts and separators.
- [Popover](popover.md): A small anchored panel for contextual controls, built on the native Popover API so it works without app state.
- [Separator](separator.md): A hairline divider, horizontal or vertical, for grouping content.

## Guidance for AI tools

Toolbar: A pill-shaped container that groups icon buttons with separators, horizontal or vertical, optionally floating in a popover. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt

# Tooltip

> Short supporting text for an unfamiliar control, shown on hover and focus with pure CSS.

- Type: Component (disclosure, Overlays)
- Namespace: `ui.tooltip`
- Source: `src/ui/tooltip.cljc`
- Public fns: `tooltip`
- Keywords: tooltip, hint, hover text, title

## When to use

- A one-line hint for an icon-only control or an abbreviation.
- Extra context that is helpful but not required to use the control.

## When not to use

- Essential information belongs in visible text; tooltips hide it from touch users.
- Use popover for rich content or anything interactive.
- Use form-field :hint for guidance under an input.

## Usage

```clojure
(require '[ui.tooltip :as tooltip])

(tooltip/tooltip {:text "Copy link"}
  (button/button {:icon :link :variant :ghost :attrs {:aria-label "Copy link"}}))
```

## API reference

### `tooltip`

Wraps children in a span that shows :text above it on hover or focus-within.

Children: The control the hint belongs to.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:text` | `string` | – | The hint. |
| `:class` | `string` | – |  |
| `:attrs` | `map` | – |  |

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Focusing the wrapped control shows the tooltip. |

## Accessibility

- The tooltip is a CSS pseudo-element, so it is not read by screen readers; icon-only controls still need an aria-label.
- Hover reveal is gated to hover-capable pointers so touch users do not get a double-tap.

## Motion

- Fades and lifts in over --duration-fast.

## Responsive behavior

- Hidden on touch devices; never place required information in a tooltip.

## Targets

- **Hiccup (`:clj`)**: Static markup, works without JS.
- **Replicant (`:cljs`)**: :class may be a vector.
- **Squint (`:squint`)**: Static markup.

## Notes for AI

- Keep the text to a few words; no punctuation at the end.
- Prefer a visible label when space allows.

## Related

- [Popover](popover.md): A small anchored panel for contextual controls, built on the native Popover API so it works without app state.
- [Button](button.md): A single action with quiet secondary states, press feedback and a loading spinner.
- [Icon](icon.md): Inline Lucide-style SVG icons in four sizes, outlined by default with filled variants for media controls.

## Guidance for AI tools

Tooltip: Short supporting text for an unfamiliar control, shown on hover and focus with pure CSS. Use only the documented props; `:class` and `:attrs` are for layout and extra attributes, never for restyling internals. The same call renders on all three targets; see Targets for the per-target event and class conventions. Keep keyboard access and both themes intact.

Full library index: docs/llms.txt
